newsitem.title: UK: UK Sea Empress probe urges more government powers.
newsitem.headline: UK Sea Empress probe urges more government powers.

text.p: The government's Marine Accident Investigation Branch (MAIB) called on Friday for a review of government powers to charter ships and aircraft to minimise the environmental damage of serious marine accidents.
The call followed a probe by the agency into last February's grounding of the Sea Empress oil tanker off Milford Haven, south Wales, in which some 70,000 tonnes of oil spilled into the sea.

The MAIB said the Transport Department should look at "the possibility of standing commercial arrangements to allow the immediate release of...vessels, aircraft and equipment" in the event of a serious incident.
"Commercial considerations should not be allowed to undermine the most expeditious actions to prevent or limit pollution," it said in a statement.

"In this respect, it is considered desirable that during a national marine emergency, the (Transport Department's) Marine Pollution Control Unit should have considerable authority to intervene in commercial negotiation to acquire equipment quickly enough."

However, the MAIB said it recognised that there were cost implications to the government taking extra powers as it would have to carry some, if not all, of the commercial risk." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
